key_insight: Neptuna is the first large-scale benchmark built specifically to stress-test machine learning surrogates on shock-driven compressible multiphase flows, and it shows that no single model or loss dominates across all settings.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark helps identify surrogate models and training strategies that better preserve interfaces, shocks, and spectral structure for practical bubble-collapse and droplet-breakup simulations.
method: Built a 2.4 TB benchmark with high-fidelity 2D and 3D datasets for bubble collapse and droplet breakup.
Compared convolutional, spectral, transformer-based, and pre-trained PDE foundation models.
Tested MSE plus composite losses with Sobolev, interface-aware, and structure-aware terms, including SoftAdapt and GradNorm.
evidence_signal: Evaluation spans pointwise, spectral, feature-focused, structural, and physics-informed metrics, with results showing composite losses improve interface preservation and spectral fidelity.
watch_item: Performance gains may depend strongly on dataset type and metric choice, so improvements on the benchmark may not transfer uniformly to other multiphase flow regimes.
paper_title: Neptuna: A Comprehensive Machine Learning Framework for Benchmarking Complex Multiphase Flows
